Subject: Renewal discussion: term + capacity increase

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the continued partnership — our renewal window for FastRetail is coming up mid-October and we
need to align on term and capacity. Over the past 12 months our usage has grown ~2.6x and we expect that to
continue as we roll the recommendation feature into two more product lines.

What we'd like to discuss:
- A price-hold for 12–24 months to give us predictability during the rollout.
- Reserved capacity for peak traffic windows (we anticipate several short bursts per month).
- An upsell path so we can increase committed capacity without long legal renegotiations.

Can you share structured options (tiered discounts, credits for onboarding or migration, invoice/true-up cadence)?
Procurement has asked for a clear mutual action plan and a PO-ready summary. I looped them (procurement@fastretail.com).

Appreciate a fast turnaround — ideally a packet we can take to our CFO next week.

Best,
Lucy Han
Director, Platform Engineering
FastRetail

--
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, procurement@fastretail.com

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: term + capacity increase

Hi Lucy — thanks for the context and the timeline. I pulled together three concise options so procurement and your CFO can evaluate trade-offs quickly. I attached a short PDF (Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf) with the numbers and a one-page mutual action plan.

High level options (summary):

Option 1 — Short term certainty (Minimal commit)- Term: 12 months- Commit: 20% uplift vs current run-rate (no reserved GPUs)- Pricing: 10% off list on committed tier; paygo rates above commit- Credits: $10k one-time onboarding credit- Pros: Low legal friction, flexible- Cons: Limited unit economics improvement for FastRetail

Option 2 — Price-hold + reserved cadence (Preferred for rollout)- Term: 24 months price-hold window- Commit: 2x current run-rate reserved capacity (guaranteed throughput pools)- Pricing: 18% commit discount + guaranteed per-token price-hold for 24 months- Credits: $50k migration credit applied over first quarter; 30 days of prioritized onboarding support- True-up: Quarterly true-up with 30-day invoice cadence- Pros: Predictable spend, capacity guarantees for peak windows- Cons: Longer term commitment, requires internal approval for credit allocation

Option 3 — No-commit flexibility (Burst-first)- Term: 12 months- Commit: none; access to burst pool with pre-negotiated capped overage rates- Pricing: list paygo rates with a capped surcharge for burst usage; 7% volume rebate if month-over-month growth exceeds threshold- Credits: $5k migration credit

Open items we need from FastRetail to finalize: current 90-day rolling run-rate, expected % of traffic that must be reserved for SLAs, and preferred billing cadence.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm which option most closely aligns with CFO appetite.
2) If Option 2 preferred, I will route to Pricing & Finance to request the $50k migration credit and the reserved capacity SKU activation.
3) We set a 30-min call to finalize MOA and signature path.

If helpful, Marissa can draft the amendment language and Ben can scope the reserved capacity ramp. Kim can confirm billing/PO mechanics for your procurement team.

Thanks — attaching the proposal.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
